title: Poll: Le Pen begins presidential campaign in strongest position ever amid worried, angry electorate
subhead: In France's polarized political landscape, Marine Le Pen of the far-right Rassemblement National is enjoying unprecedented support, and radical left candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon is building a strong base. Wide open for other candidates, the race is drawing significant interest from voters concerned about the future, Le Monde's first poll shows.

Political scientist Julia Reuschenbach: 'I do not see Chancellor Friedrich Merz resigning'
subhead: Following the Alternative for Germany (AfD) victory in Saxony-Anhalt on September 6, pressure is mounting on Chancellor Friedrich Merz's party, the Christian Democratic Union (CDU), to ease its policy of excluding the far right. Doing so would be a strategic mistake, says political scientist Julia Reuschenbach, who argues that the AfD's goal is to destroy the CDU.

title: Scottish, Welsh, Northern Irish parties to hold independence summit
subhead: The leaders of the separatist parties will hold rare talks on Monday with the aim of advancing their campaigns to break away from Britain. The meeting comes days after US President Donald Trump said he would back a united Ireland – a scenario British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has ruled out.

title: Had enough of the ham-and-cheese classic? Five places in the Paris region serving vegetarian crêpes
subhead: With onion confit, roasted carrots or artichokes, here is our selection of restaurants in and around Paris where you can enjoy delicious meat- and fish-free galettes.

title: Maha Al-Daya, the Gaza embroiderer who resists with needle and thread
subhead: Now a refugee in France, Maha Al-Daya fled the bombings that have been striking the Palestinian enclave since October 2023. To preserve the experiences of Gaza's people, she uses an ancient embroidery technique to recreate the evacuation maps dropped by the Israeli army. It is an act of resistance and resilience, stitching the memory of her homeland into fabric.

title: 25 French jihadists held in Iraq appeal to EU human rights court for repatriation
subhead: The Islamic State group members had been quietly transferred from Syria to Iraq, where they could face the death penalty. Their lawyers say Paris's refusal to prosecute them in France undermines the rule of law and opens to arbitrary decisions by the authorities.
